title: 2025-08-12 Roadmap / Launch Readiness & Incident Review
topics: Incident review: Aug 8 KV cache outage
summary: Internal roadmap and launch readiness review focused on the upcoming 2.1 release. Covered a recent KV cache incident, mitigations, and final canary rollout plan. Agreed on gating criteria for increasing traffic and a short list of action items (runbook updates, extended perf tests, canary monitoring dashboards).
transcript:
Header: 2025-08-12 10:00 AM PT | Duration: 55 min | Attendees: Priya, Ethan, Maya, Connor, Zoe, Liam

[00:00] Priya: Good morning team, thanks for joining, I think we've got about 55 minutes. main agenda: launch readiness for 2.1, quick incident review from Friday, and finalize canary thresholds.

[00:18] Ethan: yeah, i'll start with eng readiness; most tickets are green in the board, workload shaping change is merged but not in prod yet. there is one unstable test in streaming that Zoe flagged.

[00:35] Zoe: yep, the streaming flake — it seems to happen under long seq tests, maybe memory fragmentation, reproduces in staging intermittently. i can share logs after.

[00:50] Maya: i want to call out the Aug 8 outage — the KV cache eviction loop that led to throttling. we patched the immediate issue but we need stronger backstop.

[01:05] Connor: to add, the rollback was okay but took 22 minutes; we need faster toggle. the feature flag library had a delay in evaluation on heavy load.

[01:20] Priya: let's walk through the incident quickly: cause? impacts? mitigation? long term?

[01:30] Maya: cause was a race between our batch eviction job and the compaction path. under a specific seq length distribution we observed excessive cache churn, causing the serving nodes to spin on GC and timeouts increased. errors reported in telemetry, 5xx spike across the region.

[01:55] Ethan: sounds like an interaction between the new continuous batching change and the kv cache policy. we tested batching with synthetic traces but not this mixed seq distribution. apologies on that oversight.

[02:10] Zoe: from QA perspective, we didn't have a test harness that reproduces that exact distribution; most of our synthetic loads assumed uniform sequence lengths. we should add mixed-profile trace tests.

[02:30] Priya: mitigation we deployed on Friday was to back off the eviction aggressiveness and disable the compaction path. that stopped the churn but lowers hit rate. are we comfortable shipping with that mitigant in place?

[02:45] Maya: short answer yes if we can quantify the perf delta and have fallbacks. the SLA impact is small but present.

[03:00] Liam: for rollout plan, i propose a staged canary: 5% for 1 hour, monitor latency p95, error rate, cache hit ratio, if stable 15% for 3 hours, then 50% for 6 hours, then ramp. any objections?

[03:20] Connor: we should gate each step on SLOs: p95 < 220ms and 5xx < 0.2% and cache hit delta < 5 percentage points. also automated rollback on alert.

[03:38] Ethan: agree on thresholds, but i want an intermediate check at 10% for 2 hours; our prior rollout spiked at 12% so let's be cautious.

[03:50] Priya: okay so updated canary: 5%/1h, 10%/2h, 25%/4h, 50%/6h then full. monitor p95, 5xx, cache hit. publish dashboard changes.

[04:05] Maya: i'll own the monitoring dashboard updates and alerts. will add an automatic slack alert + pager if thresholds exceeded.

[04:18] Zoe: QA will run extended perf tests in staging ramping concurrency and mixed seq distributions today and tomorrow. will upload results to shared spreadsheet.

[04:30] Connor: release infra: i'll prep the canary workflows and automated rollback. need to ensure the feature flag toggle can flip in < 30s, will work with eng on a hotfix.

[04:45] Ethan: eng will push a small change to reduce the compaction contention and add a guard to the eviction job; will try to land by EOD tomorrow.

[05:00] Priya: docs and runbooks — who is updating postmortem and runbook?

[05:08] Maya: i'll draft the incident postmortem and initial runbook updates today. Zoe please add QA repro steps.

[05:18] Zoe: will do. also will add the new perf scenarios as test cases.

[05:28] Priya: ok next, external comms — do we need customer-facing notes? this was internal but a small number of customers saw degraded perf; Connor any ask from support?

[05:40] Connor: support triaged low-level tickets, no escalations. recommend a short status note to accounts for customers with dedicated stacks. can be a canned email.

[05:50] Priya: good. final check: release blockers?

[06:00] Ethan: final blocker is the streaming flake fix and the feature flag evaluation latency fix. both targeted tomorrow.

[06:12] Zoe: qa will verify flake fix in staging tests by tomorrow afternoon.

[06:25] Priya: great. let's summarize next steps and owners.

[06:32] Liam: quick question: timeline for full rollout if all gates pass?

[06:36] Priya: assuming actions complete, we can start canary on Thursday morning, and reach broad rollout by Friday close of business if stable.

[06:47] Ethan: sounds good.

[06:50] Priya: thanks everyone. we'll reconvene if alerts fire or otherwise do a quick sync after the first canary step.

[06:58] End of meeting.

Notes: transcription contains typical auto-transcription errors (names sometimes mis-attributed), timestamps approximate. Links referenced during call: shared perf spreadsheet (link: /shared/2.1-perf-results), draft postmortem doc (link: /docs/postmortem-2025-08-08-kv-cache).
